visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) Three young women walk playfully along an outdoor path beside a large green sign displaying the text 'Aquamarine Fukushima' in Japanese. One woman in a beige sweater piggybacks another in a white coat, while a third walks beside them. The setting is bright and overcast. (2) The scene shifts to an indoor aquarium where colorful tropical fish swim in large tanks filled with coral. Close-up shots follow of pink jellyfish pulsating in dark water and large crabs on a sandy tank floor. (3) An informational panel titled 'Largest Octopus' is briefly shown, followed by a detailed close-up of a giant octopus's suckers and head within a dark tank. Then, small birds known as puffins swim and dive in a water-filled exhibit. (4) A seal is seen swimming vertically inside a tall cylindrical glass tank. One of the women, wearing a beige beanie, uses her smartphone to film a fish at the water's surface. A large brown sea lion is shown perched on a rocky indoor structure, barking loudly with its mouth wide open. (5) A rapid montage features clips from a television variety show where several people in a studio setting are talking and laughing excitedly. (6) The three main women individually perform a 'shouting challenge' outdoors. Each takes a turn shouting loudly toward the camera with varying facial expressions of effort and amusement. (7) The video concludes with a group shot of the three women imitating the barking sea lion in front of a large mural of the same animal.

(2) The BGM continues as several female voices speak in high-pitched, enthusiastic Mandarin, commenting on marine life. Bubbling water sounds are faintly audible. (3) A sudden, high-intensity raspy animal bark from a sea lion interrupts the mix, followed by echoes and brief silence. (4) The audio transitions to a compressed variety show recording. Fast Mandarin dialogue, studio laughter, and exaggerated vocal reactions are dominant. (5) The original acoustic BGM resumes. Three female voices take turns performing loud, strained shouts that peak in intensity before breaking into laughter. (6) A final sequence alternates the sea lion's loud bark with the group's coordinated shout, ending in a bright piano chord and fading laughter.
